notes.text: The section is exact. This digital Yalkut reads Zeira and has bar bereih, grandson of R. Avtolos. Heilprin inserts bar but retains Ezra in his own headword.
Heilprin separates the first bar in a parenthesis. Together bar bereih means grandson. Preserve the form of his report and spell out what combining the two words yields.
Menachot contains both tenth-generation statements. The comparison records the text’s genealogy rather than establishing the pedigree independently.
Rashi identifies R. Elazar ben Azaryah as the person who was tenth from Ezra the scribe.
The distinct Perida article follows the printed paragraph about R. Pergori within the same pinned entry. Menachot describes Ezra at the door; the discussion confirms his learning.
The exact fourfold mighty-one saying is delivered by Ezra to Perida, as Rashi confirms.
The scanned source at the Elazar ben Azaryah article presents a father reading and a tenth-descendant reading, with the Ammi argument. The additional location cited in brackets is a separate lead.
The responsum agrees with Azaryah for the given name, but gives grandson of Avtolos and tenth from Elazar, rather than calling him Elazar’s father.
The same Menachot folio shows Perida asking R. Ammi a question about offerings. This attests the relationship used in the author’s chronological argument.
Berakhot expressly names Elazar ben Azaryah as tenth from Ezra.
The assessment of confusion belongs to Heilprin, who reconstructs Yuchasin’s main intention.
The conjecture about what Maimonides read is reported rather than demonstrated by his own text.
Eruvin tells of the award of four hundred additional years in a narrative about teaching. It does not establish a historical lifespan or a birth date.
The checked edition gives Azaryah in parentheses and Ezra in brackets, followed by grandson of Avtolos.
In his concluding contrast Heilprin gives ben Avtolos. The inspected Bavli instead has bar bereih, while agreeing with the headword Ezra.
The direct Yuchasin comparison matches the Elazar article. The exact second reference and its division remain uncollated.
